articles.title: HappyGF: I Built an AI Assistant to Make Sure Contractors Get Paid on Friday
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle. Every Friday, the accountant processes payments to the contractors and suppliers who keep my girlfriend's busin…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle . What I Built Every Friday, the accountant processes payments to the contractors and suppliers who keep my girlfriend's business running. For that to happen, invoices need to be received, reviewed, approved, correctly named, and forwarded to the accountant before the deadline. It sounds straightforward, until you consider how many invoices arrive by email, often from different contractors, in different formats, with different naming conventions—or none at all. The accountant requires PDF filenames containing the vendor, property, and invoice amount, following a specific convention. My girlfriend was spending far too much time opening attachments, checking details, renaming files, and forwarding them.
articles.author: Mariano Barcia

articles.title: A Raspberry Pi 3 as a mainnet validator — what a 1 GB board teaches a blockchain node
articles.excerpt: I run a small Layer-1 called Janzeer: stake-free BFT, 15-second slots, two voting rounds, finality in one block. The four last week. This post is about the fifth validator. The founding validators are…
articles.body: I run a small Layer-1 called Janzeer: stake-free BFT, 15-second slots, two voting rounds, finality in one block. The four founding validators live on one 2 GB VPS, and I wrote about that box last week . This post is about the fifth validator. It is a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B from 2016 — four Cortex-A53 cores at 1.2 GHz, 1 GB of RAM of which 905 MB are usable, a USB disk, and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi in a flat with thick walls. It has produced blocks on mainnet since 2026-10-15, and finding out what it could not do fixed seven bugs in the node that four comfortable servers had never shown. No token talk, as before; the coin is not on any exchange. Why bother The founding validators are meant to phase out.

articles.title: Articulate Me: Duolingo, but for talking
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle I don't pay for things online. Ever. Free tier, free trial, cancel before it renews, that's me. Except once. I p…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built I don't pay for things online. Ever. Free tier, free trial, cancel before it renews, that's me. Except once. I paid for an intro to data science course, because I wanted to get better at what I do. And it turns out I'm not alone: online education is projected to be a $199 billion market this year. People don't pay for apps. They pay to grow. So when this week's theme asked "what would someone actually pay for?" , I asked myself and my friends a different question: What does everyone actually want to learn? Not a programming language. Not a new tool. Every answer, in some form, came back to the same thing: how to communicate. Here's the thing nobody says out loud.

articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle A tattoo inquiry usually shows up as a vague DM: "small fox on my forearm, kinda fine line, budget around 400Rs,…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built A tattoo inquiry usually shows up as a vague DM: "small fox on my forearm, kinda fine line, budget around 400Rs, need it before the 20th." Size, references and exact placement are often missing, and some requests are things the artist simply doesn't do. Answering every one by hand takes time, and so does saying no. QueueInk is an inquiry desk for solo tattoo artists. The artist sets their own rules once: styles they don't do, placements they avoid, a minimum price, and whether they take cover-ups. Then they paste an inquiry and get: Flags from their own rules. These are checked by plain code, not by the AI.

articles.title: Letting an AI Agent Drive Ghidra: A Hands-On Test of REA’s 170 MCP Tools, One Recovered Password, and the Limits
articles.excerpt: Author: Guangyi Zhao Reverse-engineering an unfamiliar binary the traditional way means sitting in front of Ghidra, paging through assembly, following cross-references, guessing what each function doe…
articles.body: Author: Guangyi Zhao Date: 2026-10-13 Subject: morluto/rea (REA: Reverse Engineer Anything), npm package rea-agents 6.4.0, MIT license Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux x64), Node 24.20; target is an ELF built from my own C source 1. Problem and background Reverse-engineering an unfamiliar binary the traditional way means sitting in front of Ghidra, paging through assembly, following cross-references, guessing what each function does, and writing the conclusions down by hand. The slowness is not even the worst part. The worst part is how easily conclusions drift away from evidence: three days later I reread my own notes and cannot reconstruct what I actually saw when I wrote a given claim. REA proposes a different division of labor. It does not implement decompilation itself.

There are a few seasonal strips and arcs scattered across its nine-year run, sure, and Calvin's struggle with staying good before Christmas is an annual tradition. But as a whole, C&H is less concerned with the holiday calendar than one might expect, particularly in its late, post- sabbatical era.

articles.title: 10 NES Games That Are Still Worth Playing From Start to Finish
articles.excerpt: From start to finish, these 10 NES games reward every second of the time you invest in them, even decades after the fact.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1985, Nintendo released the Nintendo Entertainment System in North America alongside a limited selection of games like Super Mario Bros. and Excitebike . Within a few years, it had a library of hundreds of titles, proving that rumors of the video game industry’s death throughout the early ‘80s were greatly exaggerated. Today, many of those early games feel like antiques. They’re not nearly as memorable as they once were, with so many generations of newer software to choose from. But there are some that still deserve your attention, even now. Here are 10 NES games that are still worth playing from start to finish.

articles.title: 9 Best DLCs That Were Even Better Than the Base Game
articles.excerpt: From Hell weddings to alien hive-minds, these nine DLCs took a hard swerve away from the games they built off.
articles.body: Even the wildest DLC needs a solid game to swerve away from, or the swerve doesn’t land. Every base game with excellent DLC is strong enough to stand on its own. That’s the common DNA: studios that had built something sturdy enough to trust it, confident enough to hand players a portal to hell, an alien hive-mind under a suburban cul-de-sac, or a crown that makes you ruler of an entire realm of madness — and bet that players would play anyway. For these nine DLCs, that confidence turned out to be well-placed. Here are the best DLCs of all time that took their main story and had the confidence to dream up wild new experiences for dedicated players. Each of these nine game expansions took a big swing, and has been remembered for that creativity ever since.

articles.excerpt: Japan's mission to Mars' moons could answer a decades old question dividing the origins of Phobos and Deimos between two conflicting theories, and make history as the first spacecraft to return to Ear…
articles.body: Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system. The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. The robust undertaking includes a landing on Phobos to collect the samples — which will likely be the first from the Mars system to return to Earth — and a search for evidence that could shed light on events during the formation of the solar system billions of years ago. articles.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering programmer who helped NASA land Apollo astronauts on the moon. But we will always have her example to inspire us.
articles.body: Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 18, 1963: France's Félicette Becomes the 1st Cat in Space! >^..^<
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

articles.body: Spain is one of the easiest places in the world to experience the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. Excellent roads, plentiful accommodation and Málaga's international airport make this an obvious alternative to North Africa and the Middle East. However, choosing where to watch requires some thought.

articles.excerpt: The Artemis II crew have joined an impressive list of honourees, including Buzz Aldrin, Jane Goodall and David Attenborough.
articles.body: TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — The Artemis II astronauts may have traveled hundreds of thousands of miles away from Earth to the moon, but they made sure the rest of us didn't miss out on the adventure. Now, their efforts to bring the wonders of space exploration back down to Earth have earned them one of science communication's most prestigious honors: the Stephen Hawking Medal. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover , alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen , accepted the award on Saturday (Oct. 17), during the opening ceremony of the Starmus VIII festival. The honor recognizes all four crew members, including NASA astronaut Christina Koch , who wasn't in attendance.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
